Emotional Intelligence & Brain Dynamics

The Triune Brain Model, The Amygdala Hijack & EQ vs. IQ in Tech Leadership

Academic Lead:Mrs. Ishara Raviharee Weerasinghe(Senior Lecturer in English | Lecturer In Charge)
SLIIT City Uni • Professional Skills Assessment Standard
Curriculum Overview & Context

Grounds emotional intelligence in evolutionary neuroscience. Analyzes Paul MacLean's Triune Brain Model, Daniel Goleman's Amygdala Hijack mechanism, Paul Ekman's 6 universal emotions, and the comparative value of EQ over IQ.

Core Competencies & Learning Objectives

  • →Understand the three evolutionary layers of Paul MacLean's Triune Brain Model.
  • →Identify the neurobiological mechanism of the Amygdala Hijack and apply the 6-to-10 second respiration pause.
  • →Recognize Paul Ekman's 6 hard-wired universal human emotions.
  • →Contrast Emotional Quotient (EQ) and Intelligence Quotient (IQ) in career advancement.
  • →Develop the 4 core domains of EQ: Self-Awareness, Self-Management, Social Awareness, and Relationship Management.

Neuroscience Foundation: The Triune Brain Model

The Three Evolutionary Strata of Human Cognition

Developed by neuroscientist Paul MacLean, the Triune Brain Model conceptualizes the human brain as three distinct, evolutionarily layered systems that cooperate (and frequently clash) under pressure.

1. Reptilian Complex (Brainstem & Cerebellum):The oldest evolutionary layer (~500 million years old). Controls autonomic physical functions (heart rate, breathing) and instinctual survival drives: fight, flight, or freeze.
2. Limbic System (Mammalian Brain — Amygdala & Hippocampus):Evolved in early mammals (~150 million years old). The seat of emotions, social bonding, memory encoding, and rapid threat appraisal. Prioritizes immediate emotional survival over logic.
3. Neocortex (Prefrontal Cortex — 'The CEO'):The newest evolutionary development. Responsible for rational logic, abstract deduction, architectural planning, impulse inhibition, and ethical decision-making.

The Amygdala Hijack Mechanism (Goleman, 1995)

How Stress Short-Circuits Executive Function

When sensory input enters the brain via the thalamus, it splits into two pathways: a slow, high-resolution route to the Neocortex for rational processing, and a high-speed emergency shortcut to the Amygdala.

When emotional stimuli are perceived as threats (e.g., severe critical feedback from a tech lead), the amygdala triggers an immediate flood of adrenaline and cortisol before the prefrontal cortex can process the data.

This causes an 'Amygdala Hijack'—irrational outbursts, defensive panic, or cognitive shutdown.

The 6-to-10 Second Respiration Protocol
“Neurological research demonstrates that an amygdala hormonal surge lasts between 6 and 10 seconds. Taking slow, deep diaphragmatic breaths during this critical window replenishes prefrontal oxygenation, allowing the rational 'CEO' to regain command before you speak or act.”
— Daniel Goleman

Paul Ekman's 6 Universal Emotions & EQ vs. IQ

Hard-Wired Biology and Workplace Performance

Psychologist Paul Ekman demonstrated across diverse global cultures that all human beings share six primary, biologically hard-wired emotions: Joy, Anger, Disgust, Fear, Sadness, and Surprise.

In the knowledge workplace, IQ gets an engineer hired for technical skills, but EQ determines whether they can lead teams, resolve conflicts, withstand sprint pressure, and earn executive trust.

AttributeEmotional Intelligence (EQ)Intelligence Quotient (IQ)
Cognitive FocusUnderstanding, regulating, and harnessing emotions effectively.Logical reasoning, mathematical ability, and abstract spatial retention.
Plasticity Over LifetimeDynamically expandable throughout life through deliberate practice.Relatively static after late adolescence and early adulthood.
Workplace PredictorPredicts leadership trajectory, stress resilience, and team cohesion.Predicts baseline technical comprehension and raw coding speed.
Crisis PerformanceEnables calm de-escalation, empathy, and psychological safety.Can break down into defensive paralysis during emotional conflict.

Neuroscience Intervention Protocol

The 6-to-10 Second Amygdala De-escalation Pause

When triggered by harsh criticism or stress, an amygdala hormone surge floods the bloodstream for 6 to 10 seconds. Deep diaphragmatic respiration allows the Neocortex (CEO) to regain cognitive control before reacting impulsively.

Connecting Theory to Practice: Undergraduate & Developer

Reflective analysis connecting Emotional Intelligence & Brain Dynamics to coursework at SLIIT City Uni, software engineering projects (LA'CEDRA, TechMart, ApPoint), digital systems at LA'CEDRA, and collaborative teamwork.

01. Meaning & Conceptual Core

Emotional Intelligence (EQ) is the capacity to recognize, understand, regulate, and harness emotions in oneself and in interactions with others. Grounded in evolutionary neuroscience (Paul MacLean's Triune Brain Model) and cognitive psychology (Daniel Goleman), it explains how emotional stimuli can trigger an 'Amygdala Hijack' and provides physiological strategies to restore prefrontal executive control.

02. Key Theoretical Concepts Acquired
→The Triune Brain Model (Paul MacLean): Reptilian Complex (autonomic survival instincts), Limbic System (mammalian emotional seat / amygdala), and Neocortex (human rational CEO / prefrontal logic).
→The Amygdala Hijack Mechanism (Daniel Goleman): When high-stress stimuli bypass rational prefrontal processing, triggering immediate defensive aggression or panic.
→The 6-to-10 Second Respiration Interruption: Conscious deep breathing recalibrates physiological oxygenation, allowing the prefrontal cortex to re-engage cognitive command.
→The 4 Core Domains of Emotional Intelligence: Self-Awareness (emotional radar), Self-Management (self-control & adaptability), Social Awareness (organizational empathy), and Relationship Management (constructive mediation).
→Comparative Dynamics: IQ predicts baseline technical learning and logic; EQ determines leadership trajectory, collaborative durability, and stress tolerance.
→Paul Ekman's 6 Hard-Wired Universal Emotions: Joy, Anger, Disgust, Fear, Sadness, and Surprise.
IT//EQ
03. Industry Imperative — Why This Matters in Tech

Software development environments are high-stress pressure cookers characterized by critical production outages, unforgiving deployment deadlines, and contentious code disputes. An engineer who succumbs to amygdala hijacks becomes toxic, defensive, and resistant to constructive feedback, creating team burnout and technical debt.

05. Practical Workplace & Venture Applications

Scenario 1:Handling Critical Software Code Reviews or Architectural Disagreements

Recognizing physiological fight-or-flight triggers (racing pulse, shallow breathing) when code is challenged; taking three deep diaphragmatic breaths to re-engage the prefrontal cortex before responding constructively.

Scenario 2:Navigating High-Pressure Deployment Setbacks at LA'CEDRA

Maintaining calm executive composure when faced with unexpected build errors or tight delivery deadlines, focusing on systematic analytical debugging rather than venting frustration on team members.

08. Personal Key Takeaways

01.An Amygdala Hijack is a physiological impulse, but reacting defensively is an executive choice; breathe for 6–10 seconds to restore rational command.
02.IQ gets an engineer hired for technical capability, but EQ determines whether they can lead teams, mediate disputes, and endure corporate crises.

Core Academic Takeaways

01.

The Triune Brain consists of the Reptilian Complex (survival), Limbic System (emotion), and Neocortex (rational CEO).

02.

The Amygdala Hijack occurs when emotional stimuli bypass rational thinking; a 6-to-10 second respiration pause restores executive control.

03.

Paul Ekman identified 6 hard-wired emotions: Joy, Anger, Disgust, Fear, Sadness, and Surprise.

04.

EQ > IQ in the modern tech industry: technical skills solve code problems, but emotional intelligence solves human collaboration challenges.

Academic Literature & Primary Citations (APA 7th)

Goleman, D. (1995). Emotional Intelligence: Why It Can Matter More Than IQ. Bantam Books.

Detailed evolutionary neuroscience monograph mapping the phylogenetic development of the human brain.
